# Welcome {.unnumbered}

This is an open access textbook on personality psychology. It asks what
personality differences actually are, how we know they exist, where they come
from, and what they do — and it tries to be honest about how much of that we
can currently answer.

## About This Book

Most introductions to personality begin and end with description: here are the
Big Five, here is how we measure them, here is what they predict. Description
is where this book starts too, but it is not where it stops. I treat trait
models as useful abstractions rather than as facts about how the mind is built,
and spend most of the book asking what sits underneath them.

The organizing idea comes from the first chapter: questions about behavior can
be asked at different levels, and answers at one level do not substitute for
answers at another. Knowing that a trait is heritable is not the same as
knowing what it is for, and knowing what it is for is not the same as knowing
how it works. With that framing in place, the book works through historical and
contemporary perspectives, measurement, and how much personality actually
predicts, then turns to causes and mechanisms — evolution, genetics,
physiology, emotion, and motivation. It closes with how personality develops
over a life, how it varies across cultures, and whether it can be deliberately
changed.

The book assumes no prior background beyond an introductory psychology course.
